observations.observation: The entry point precisely limits use to Northstar Relay incident assessment, requires the routing reference for every assessment, conditionally loads delivery-state meanings, preserves precedence, and specifies all six output sections.
The entry point defines equally precise scope boundaries, ordered rule evaluation, uncertainty behavior, conditional reference loading, and the six-section output contract.

The result selects signature-integrity and P1, treats HTTP 429 as secondary, stops retries, keeps the delivery quarantined, identifies the missing active signing-key identifier, and cites NSR-AUTH-17 and NSR-MISSING-08.
The result reaches the same source-faithful route and makes the non-retryability of the 120-second value explicit, with applicable rule explanations and no forbidden lower-precedence classification.

cases.explanation: Both packages are valid, compact, source-faithful, and operationally clear, and both downstream assessments satisfy the held-out contract without repair. Their presentation differences do not create an observable downstream advantage, so the exact tie rule applies.

observations.observation: A keeps a concise 35-line entry point and directs the agent to a dedicated evidence-policy reference for detailed hierarchy, claim classification, citation, qualifier, and enforcement rules.

B places the full hierarchy, classification procedure, qualifier rules, citation contract, stop conditions, and enforcement discussion in a 122-line always-loaded entry point rather than partitioning detailed policy.

A includes all three supported evidence identifiers, preserves every required acceptance qualifier, withholds all unsupported marketing claims, and separately records the request to omit lab qualifiers with a concrete reason.

B accurately drafts the supported changes and withholds the universal reliability, zero-loss, speed, and mobile-continuation claims, but it does not separately disclose the explicit request to omit material lab qualifiers.

cases.explanation: Both arms are accurate and pass the critical gate, but A is better partitioned and its downstream artifact is more inspectable and complete because it discloses the qualifier-removal request instead of silently omitting it. That observable downstream advantage and the three-point total margin support an A verdict.

overallNotes: No critical failures were found. The webhook case is a substantive tie; A wins release-evidence on package partitioning and downstream disclosure completeness.
